notes:
Here are the verse-by-verse notes on Daniel 2:1-24. I used Enduring Word (Guzik), Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Calvin, Matthew Henry, Barnes, Gill, Pulpit, Constable, Wesley and Jerome. I couldn't find pages from bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org, newadvent.org, catholic.com or oca.org, and nothing on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching for this passage, so none of that is here.

**v. 1**
- **"Second year":** Guzik says the timing is hard to pin down. Babylonian ways of counting reign years overlapped, so 602 BC could be both the king's second year and the end of the three years of training. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB's answer: Nebuchadnezzar first ruled under his father, Nabopolassar (that's chapter 1). "Second year" here counts from when he ruled alone. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Clarke likewise counts it as his second year of ruling alone. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/clarke/daniel/2.htm
- **"Dreams" (plural):** It was one dream with many parts. The Geneva notes, Wesley and Calvin all say so. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/2-1.htm ; https://ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Daniel.html ; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html
- **Why the king got the dream:** JFB says a dream suited someone outside God's kingdom, as with Pharaoh. But an Israelite interprets it, so the glory goes to God. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- **Application:** Matthew Henry says that if we could see into the hearts of the powerful, we would pity them rather than envy them. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_002.cfm

**v. 2**
- **The four groups:** Constable describes them. The magicians were scholars who claimed to read the future. The enchanters claimed to contact the dead. The sorcerers cast spells. The "Chaldeans" were a priestly caste who studied the stars. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/daniel-2.html
- Jerome gives his own definitions of the groups. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/pearse/morefathers/files/jerome_daniel_02_text.htm
- **Who sent the dream:** Calvin says the king's terror shows he sensed that God had sent it. God would not let him rest until he had the meaning. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html

**v. 3**
- Calvin says the king admits he doesn't understand. The wise men should have been afraid, yet they confidently promised an answer. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html
- JFB says the king woke alarmed and couldn't recall what the dream looked like. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 4**
- **The switch to Aramaic:** From 2:4 to 7:28 the book is written in Aramaic, the language of the Babylonian empire. Guzik notes it is one of only three Aramaic sections in the Bible. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB says the Aramaic part deals with the Gentile powers, while the Hebrew parts deal more with the Jews. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Constable says the same: these chapters concern matters of worldwide interest. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dcc/daniel-2.html
- **"Chaldeans" and the book's date:** Guzik reports that critics see this use of the word as a mistake only a 2nd-century-BC writer would make. He replies that the Babylonian word for astrologer-priest and the name of the people sounded alike. That critical view is the only modern-scholarship position I found, and only as Guzik reports it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/

**v. 5: the main disputed point**
The question is whether the king *forgot* the dream ("the thing is gone from me," KJV) or *announced a fixed decision* ("my word is final," BSB). This is a debate between individual scholars, not between denominations.
- **Forgot it:** Barnes holds this view. Note that the magicians took it that way and the king didn't correct them. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/2-5.htm
- Trapp also takes it this way: the king dreamed of kingdoms and forgot it, a lesson that kingdoms are empty bubbles. https://studylight.org/commentaries/jtc/daniel-2.html
- **Fixed decree:** Pulpit translates it "the word which has gone forth from me is fixed." On this view the king refuses to tell the dream as a test, not because he has forgotten it. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/daniel-2.html
- Another note quoted on the Bible Hub page goes further. It calls the word Persian, meaning "sure," and says the rendering "gone" can't be defended. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/daniel/2-5.htm
- Precept Austin calls "the matter is gone from me" incorrect. https://www.preceptaustin.org/daniel_2_commentary
- **Undecided:** Gill gives both readings. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wbt/daniel/2-5.html
- Calvin (Reformed) leaves the point open. https://www.ccel.org/c/calvin/comment3/comm_vol24/htm/viii.iv.htm
- Guzik suggests the king may have kept only a vague memory. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- **Was the king fair?** Calvin says no. The magi never claimed to tell people their dreams, and the king acted with "brutal rage." Still, God was using this to expose their boasting. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html
- **The punishment:** Guzik quotes Archer's description of how people were torn apart. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB says "dunghill" means a heap of mud, because mud-brick houses dissolved into mire. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 6**
- JFB says "rewards" literally means gifts poured out lavishly. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Calvin says this shows the magi made money from their predictions. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html

**v. 7**
- Calvin says the magi told the truth: their skill covered only interpreting dreams, not knowing them. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html

**v. 8**
- JFB says "gain time" literally means "buy time." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Barnes reads it as: you can see I've forgotten, so you are only stalling. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/daniel/2-8.html

**v. 9**
- **The test:** Guzik says the king couldn't check an interpretation, but he could check whether they knew the dream itself. If they were what they claimed, they should manage both. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB puts it this way: if they can't tell the past, how can they tell the future? https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- **"Till the situation changes":** JFB says this could mean until the king lost interest, or until there was a change of government. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 10**
- Jerome says the magi admit, along with all secular learning, that knowing the future belongs to God, not to humans. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/pearse/morefathers/files/jerome_daniel_02_text.htm
- Wesley (Methodist) makes the same point: since knowledge must come from God, what Daniel did wasn't human strength. https://ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Daniel.html
- Guzik says their tactic was to make the king look unreasonable rather than themselves look incompetent. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/

**v. 11**
- **The gods "not with mortals":** JFB contrasts this pagan idea of a distant god with John 1:14, "the Word was made flesh." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Guzik draws the same line to Immanuel, "God with us." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- Calvin takes "the gods" to mean the many gods the magi imagined, not angels. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/daniel-2.html

**v. 12**
- Matthew Henry says that however unjust the king was, God was just. Men who pretended to do what they couldn't were condemned for failing at what they never pretended to do. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_002.cfm
- Guzik suggests a new king may have welcomed the chance to clear out his father's advisers. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/

**v. 13**
- JFB says Daniel and his friends were apparently not counted among the magi, so they weren't summoned. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Wesley says they weren't called because of their youth. https://ccel.org/w/wesley/notes/notes/Daniel.html
- Jerome says the Chaldeans deliberately kept the question from them. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/pearse/morefathers/files/jerome_daniel_02_text.htm

**v. 14**
- Guzik says Daniel's calm shows that crises don't make a person, they reveal one. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB says Arioch commanded the executioners. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 15**
- JFB takes Daniel's question to mean "why weren't we all consulted?" It shows Daniel hadn't known about the matter. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 16**
- Guzik says asking for time wasn't stalling. Daniel knew that listening to God takes time. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB, following Barnes, suggests Daniel may have asked through a courtier rather than in person. He thinks the king allowed it because Daniel, unlike the Chaldeans, didn't ask to be told the dream. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 17**
- JFB says this explains why Daniel wanted time: so his friends could pray with him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 18**
- JFB calls this an example of united prayer, as in Matthew 18:19 and Peter's rescue in Acts 12. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Matthew Henry says that when good people's lives are in danger, it is time to pray earnestly. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_002.cfm
- Guzik says the battle was won when Daniel prayed with his friends. He also notes that Joseph interpreted dreams but never reconstructed one. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/

**v. 19**
- Guzik says this was "not religion, but revelation." He isn't sure whether the "night vision" was a dream or a vision. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB sees this as one step in God gradually training Daniel for clearer revelations later in the book. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 20**
- JFB says God's "name" means God as he shows himself in his acts. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Matthew Henry notes that wisdom and strength, often separate in people, are united in God. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_002.cfm

**v. 21**
- JFB quotes Jerome: this line hints that the dream will be about kingdoms rising and falling. JFB adds that the fortunes of nations are ruled by God, not by chance or fate. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- Guzik says Daniel praises God as stronger than a mighty king like Nebuchadnezzar. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/

**v. 22**
- Guzik says God's power would help little if he stayed silent, so Daniel praises him for speaking. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- JFB links the verse to Psalm 139:11-12 and James 1:17. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**v. 23**
- **"God of my fathers":** JFB says God showed the same covenant grace to a captive exile. Daniel's "me… we… us" credits his friends' prayers. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- **"The king's matter":** JFB notes these are the exact words the Chaldeans used in v. 10 for what no one could do. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- **Faith and praise:** Guzik (Calvary Chapel, the site you listed as Pentecostal) says Daniel praised God before the answer was confirmed. He argues that greater faith praises on the promise, before the answer is in hand. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-2/
- Matthew Henry says God honoured the spirit of prophecy while shaming the spirit of divination. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Dan/Dan_002.cfm

**v. 24**
- JFB says "bring me before the king" suggests Daniel hadn't yet met the king in person. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm
- JFB adds that v. 24 shows the executions hadn't actually started when Daniel stepped in. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/daniel/2.htm

**Where Protestant traditions differ**
I found no real denominational split in verses 1-24. The Reformed (Calvin, Matthew Henry), Baptist (Gill), Methodist (Wesley) and Calvary Chapel (Guzik) sources all read the passage the same way. The live disagreements, about verse 5 and the dating in verse 1, are between individual scholars.
